summary: WI-763 meets the stated goal at the semantic level: it introduces a PR-specific required check (`loom-pr-merge-gate`) that proves fresh authored Loom semantic approval (`work_item.review_entry` with `decision: allow`) for the current PR head, fails closed on drift/bypass, and provides a controlled-merge wrapper that verifies host required-check enforcement before delegating merge. Validation evidence and installed-runtime fixtures cover the critical negative cases (missing/stale/non-allow review, raw-evidence-only bypass, and missing enforcement).

findings.summary: Host enforcement closure still requires live readback evidence that `loom-pr-merge-gate` is required on `main` (branch protection or an active ruleset); workflow presence alone is not proof.

disposition.summary: Collect and record live GitHub branch protection / ruleset readback showing `loom-pr-merge-gate` is required on `main`, and confirm a real PR head run exists for the same head SHA.

findings.details: category: unresolved; scope note: repo-local artifacts establish the mechanism, but host enforcement truth requires live host readback.

findings.summary: `.github/workflows/pr-merge-gate.yml` runs on `merge_group`, but the gate payload currently relies on inferring a unique PR from `head_sha`/branch when PR number is absent; merge-queue commits can map to multiple PRs and may fail closed unexpectedly.

disposition.summary: Either (a) remove/limit `merge_group` until the PR binding for merge queue is made deterministic, or (b) extend `pr-gate`/workflow to extract an unambiguous PR binding for merge-queue runs.

findings.details: category: new; risk: merge queue adoption could be blocked by ambiguous PR binding even when authored review truth exists.

findings.summary: `pr-gate`/`controlled-merge` read GitHub state via `gh` first, but `gh_json()` does not handle `FileNotFoundError`; environments without `gh` would crash instead of falling back to token-authenticated REST.

disposition.summary: Catch `FileNotFoundError` in `gh_json()` (and treat it as a normal error path) so the REST fallback can execute; document the runtime prerequisite if `gh` is intentionally required.

findings.details: category: new; impact: required check could fail with non-JSON output if `gh` is unavailable, causing hard-to-diagnose gate failures.
